title: Drummers: Red Happy Bolton and Mac Murray
summary: Punch recalls drummer Happy Goldston, whom he saw at the Regal Theater but never played with; Allen asks about Mac Murray.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: The one uptown now. He took the Chinese place with me, you know.
Yeah, Black Hat. Black Hat. Now, really happy. Holston? Goldston?

Goldston, yeah. Now, really happy. He was a real good drummer and everything, but I never did play with him. You know, I seen him at the Regal Theater there with Robichoke Bay. I thought he was a mighty good drummer. I thought he was a very good drummer. I thought he was a very good drummer.

I never met him. I heard Paul Balberin talk a lot about him. One of his favorites is not his favorite. Well, what did John McMurray play like? Isn't that his name? Mac Murray, they called it. I'm not sure of his first name. Did you know him? Mac Murray, the drummer. Did you ever know him? No. I never knew him.
